summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was admitted due to low-grade fevers and right upper quadrant abdominal pain, concerning for recurrent cholangitis. She was afebrile on arrival and hemodynamically stable. Initial labs showed mild abnormalities in liver enzymes and blood counts, but blood cultures were negative. She was started on IV meropenem and later transitioned to cefepime and metronidazole. Her symptoms improved during the hospitalization, and she remained afebrile. A PICC line was placed on discharge to complete a 14-day course of ertapenem at home. Her home diuretics were held due to lower-than-usual blood pressure and were not restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and instructions to follow up with the liver clinic for ongoing management.
problems: Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
